paragraphs.en: In order to “change lives for the better” and reduce “dependency”, George Osborne, Chancellor of the Exchequer, introduced the “upfront work search” scheme. Only if the jobless arrive at the jobcentre with a CV, register for online job search, and start looking for work will they be eligible for benefit – and then they should report weekly rather than fortnightly. What could be more reasonable?
paragraphs.zh: 为了“让生活变得更好”，并减少“依赖”，英国财政大臣乔治·奥斯本推出了“先求职”计划。失业者只有带着简历到就业中心报到、注册网络求职并开始找工作，才有资格领取福利；之后，他们还应每周汇报一次，而不是每两周一次。还有什么比这更合理呢？

paragraphs.en: More apparent reasonableness followed. There will now be a seven-day wait for the jobseeker’s allowance. “Those first few days should be spent looking for work, not looking to sign on,” he claimed. “We’re doing these things because we know they help people stay off benefits and help those on benefits get into work faster.” Help? Really? On first hearing, this was the socially concerned chancellor, trying to change lives for the better, complete with “reforms” to an obviously indulgent system that demands too little effort from the newly unemployed to find work, and subsidises laziness. What motivated him, we were to understand, was his zeal for “fundamental fairness” – protecting the taxpayer, controlling spending and ensuring that only the most deserving claimants received their benefits.
paragraphs.zh: 接着，又出现了更多表面上合理的措施。如今，领取求职津贴要等待七天。他宣称：“最初的那几天应该用来找工作，而不是想着登记领取救济。我们这样做，是因为我们知道，这些措施能帮助人们不依赖福利，并帮助已经领取福利的人更快找到工作。”帮助？真的吗？乍听之下，这是一位关心社会的财政大臣，正在努力改善人们的生活，并且还要对一个显然过于宽纵的制度实施“改革”：这个制度对新近失业者找工作的努力要求太少，简直是在补贴懒惰。我们被要求这样理解：激励他的，是他对“根本公平”的热忱，也就是保护纳税人、控制开支，并确保只有最应该获得福利的申请者才能领到福利。

paragraphs.en: Losing a job is hurting: you don’t skip down to the jobcentre with a song in your heart, delighted at the prospect of doubling your income from the generous state. It is financially terrifying, psychologically embarrassing and you know that support is minimal and extraordinarily hard to get. You are now not wanted; you are now excluded from the work environment that offers purpose and structure in your life. Worse, the crucial income to feed yourself and your family and pay the bills has disappeared. Ask anyone newly unemployed what they want and the answer is always: a job.
paragraphs.zh: 失去工作是痛苦的：你不会因为慷慨的国家可能让你的收入翻倍，就满心欢喜、蹦蹦跳跳地跑到就业中心。失业在经济上令人恐惧，在心理上令人难堪，而且你知道，能获得的援助微乎其微，还极难申请。如今你不再被需要；如今你被排除在工作环境之外，而工作原本赋予你的生活目标和秩序。更糟的是，那笔用来养活自己和家人、支付账单的关键收入没有了。问问任何一位刚失业的人想要什么，答案总是：一份工作。

paragraphs.en: But in Osborneland, your first instinct is to fall into dependency – permanent dependency if you can get it – supported by a state only too ready to indulge your falsehood. It is as though 20 years of ever-tougher reforms of the job search and benefit administration system never happened. The principle of British welfare is no longer that you can insure yourself against the risk of unemployment and receive unconditional payments if the disaster happens. Even the very phrase “jobseeker’s allowance” is about redefining the unemployed as a “jobseeker” who had no fundamental right to a benefit he or she has earned through making national insurance contributions. Instead, the claimant receives a time-limited “allowance,” conditional on actively seeking a job; no entitlement and no insurance, at £71.70 a week, one of the least generous in the EU.
paragraphs.zh: 但在奥斯本想象的世界里，你的第一反应是陷入依赖——如果可能，最好是永久依赖——而国家则迫不及待地纵容你的欺骗行为，为你提供供养。仿佛过去二十年间，对求职与福利管理制度日益严厉的改革从未发生过。英国福利制度的原则，早已不再是让你为失业风险投保，并在灾难来临时无条件获得给付。甚至“求职者津贴”这个名称本身，就是要把失业者重新定义为“求职者”：他们对于自己通过缴纳国民保险金所挣得的福利，已不再拥有基本权利。相反，申请者领取的是有期限的“津贴”，条件是必须积极找工作；它既不是理所应得的权利，也不是保险，每周只有71.70英镑，属于欧盟中最不优厚的水平之一。
